definition: Crude slang for sexual intercourse or a single sex act; literally 'cannon'; functions as both noun ('a fuck') and verb ('to fuck'), typically implying vigorous or casual sex.
notes: Appears in compounds 打炮 and 干炮; homophonous with but distinct from 泡 (pào, to pursue/seduce), which uses a different character.

definition: Crude slang verb meaning to have sex; literally 'fire a cannon'; typically framed from the perspective of the active or initiating partner.
notes: 打 (to strike/do) + 炮 (cannon/fuck); slightly more verb-oriented than bare 炮; common in casual male-register speech and online forums.

definition: Onomatopoeic internet slang for sexual intercourse; the triple syllable mimics the rhythmic sound of skin contact during sex; emphatic variant of 啪啪.
notes: Triple form adds emphasis relative to the double 啪啪; proliferated on Weibo and WeChat-era Chinese internet; relatively playful register that evades content filters more readily than explicit terms.

definition: Onomatopoeic internet slang for sexual intercourse; mimics the sound of skin slapping during sex; the dominant casual shorthand for sex in contemporary mainland Chinese internet discourse.
notes: Probably the single most-used casual euphemism for sex on Chinese internet platforms; onomatopoeic ambiguity makes it difficult for automated content moderation to suppress; less vulgar than 炮 or 干.

definition: Euphemistic idiom for having sex; literally 'roll the sheets'; evokes tangled bedsheets during intercourse as an indirect image of the act.
notes: Widely used in entertainment media, drama recaps, and casual speech as a humorous and relatively inoffensive reference to sex; structurally similar to English 'hit the sheets.'

definition: Euphemistic use of 'to do' for having sex; gains sexual meaning entirely from context, parallel to English 'do it'; too ambiguous to carry sexual meaning in isolation.
notes: Most commonly appears as 做爱 (zuò'ài, 'make love'); bare 做 requires unambiguous sexual context to be read sexually; the lightest and most deniable register in this set.

definition: Euphemistic use of 'to sleep' for having sex with someone; typically takes a grammatical object, as in 睡了她 ('slept with her').
notes: Near-universal cross-linguistic metaphor; the parallel to English 'sleep with' is exact in both form and register; among the mildest and most socially acceptable Mandarin euphemisms for sex.

definition: Slang verb meaning to pursue and seduce someone for sex; literally 'to soak/immerse'; emphasizes the flirtation and pursuit process rather than the sex act itself, as in 泡妞 ('pick up girls').
notes: Distinct character from 炮 (pào, cannon/fuck) despite identical romanization; 泡 focuses on the social seduction process rather than the act; implies eventual sexual success without naming it explicitly.

definition: Crude slang meaning to successfully have sex with someone; literally 'to do/mess onto someone'; the directional 上 marks completion of a goal, framing sex as a conquest.
notes: 搞 (gǎo) alone means 'to handle/mess with'; 上 as a directional complement signals achieved outcome; comparable to English 'to score' or 'to get into bed with'; implies prior pursuit followed by success.

definition: Extremely crude compound for having sex; stacks two independent crude sex terms (干 'to fuck' + 炮 'fuck/cannon') for intensified vulgarity; implies aggressive or vigorous intercourse.
notes: 干 (gàn) is itself a standalone crude verb for sex with broad recognition; combining it with 炮 doubles the vulgarity; among the highest-crude-register Mandarin terms for intercourse.

definition: Standard clinical term for oral sex; literally 'mouth intercourse'; applies to both fellatio and cunnilingus and is the dominant medical and educational term.
notes: Used in sex education curricula, public health campaigns, and mainstream media; does not distinguish fellatio from cunnilingus without additional specification; the go-to neutral term.

definition: Highly clinical term for fellatio; literally 'penis oral sex'; specifies oral stimulation of the penis as distinct from cunnilingus.
notes: 阴茎 (yīnjīng) is the clinical/anatomical term for penis; this compound appears in medical and sexological literature but is rarely used in everyday speech; low general-public recognition due to clinical register.

definition: Formal clinical term for oral sex; literally 'oral cavity sexual intercourse'; more technically precise than 口交 and encountered primarily in medical or legal documents.
notes: 口腔 (kǒuqiāng) denotes the anatomical oral cavity; the full compound is the most formally verbose Mandarin rendering of oral sex; general-public recognition is lower than 口交 due to its bureaucratic register.

definition: Euphemistic slang for fellatio; literally 'blow the xiao (a vertical bamboo flute)'; the wind-instrument metaphor for oral stimulation of the penis parallels English 'blow job.'
notes: 箫 is a traditional Chinese end-blown bamboo flute; the metaphor is widely understood; carries a faintly classical or literary register because the instrument is associated with traditional music and poetry.

definition: Slang for fellatio; literally 'blow the trumpet/horn'; a variant of the wind-instrument metaphor using a louder, brassier instrument than the xiao.
notes: 喇叭 covers trumpet, brass horn, and loudspeaker; slightly more colloquial and less classically refined than 吹箫; both terms exploit the structural parallel with English 'blow job.'

definition: Casual slang for oral sex; literally 'mouth work/activity'; can refer to either fellatio or cunnilingus; the framing emphasizes skilled performance.
notes: 活 (huó) means 'work' or 'craft,' implying technique or effort; used gender-neutrally for either direction of oral sex; common in online discussions, dating apps, and erotic literature.

definition: Slang verb for fellatio; literally 'to hold in the mouth/to contain'; acquires sexual meaning entirely from context.
notes: Primary meaning is 'to hold something in one's mouth' with no inherent sexual valence; used in erotic literature and online content where context makes the referent unambiguous; slightly more passive and receptive in feel than 吸.

definition: Slang verb for fellatio in a sexual context; literally 'to suck'; relies on context to distinguish sexual from non-sexual use.
notes: 吸 also appears in clinical contexts (e.g., 吸痰, suction of mucus); more physically active in connotation than 含; sexual meaning is purely contextual; both 含 and 吸 require co-text to be read sexually.

definition: Extremely crude slang for fellatio; literally 'lick dick'; 屌 (diǎo) is one of the most vulgar Mandarin terms for the penis.
notes: 屌 (diǎo) is roughly equivalent in vulgarity to English 'dick' at its crudest register; this compound is highly offensive in formal or public contexts; common in pornographic content and crude peer-register speech.

definition: Extremely crude slang for fellatio; literally 'eat dick'; the eating metaphor frames oral sex as consumption and structurally mirrors 吃猫 (cunnilingus).
notes: 吃 (to eat) creates a symmetrical vulgar pair with 吃猫 (cunnilingus); the eating metaphor for oral sex recurs across multiple languages; highly offensive in formal contexts.

definition: Chinese calque of English 'deep throat'; refers to fellatio in which the full length of the penis is inserted into the throat; also used as a cultural reference to the 1972 pornographic film and the Watergate informant.
notes: 深 (deep) + 喉 (throat); borrowed as a direct morpheme-for-morpheme translation of the English term; carries the same dual-register resonance as in English — both sexual act and political informant metaphor.

definition: Clinical term for cunnilingus; literally 'genital/vulvar oral sex'; the most formally precise Mandarin term for this act.
notes: 阴部 (yīnbù) refers broadly to the external genital area; highest clinical register for this act in Mandarin; encountered primarily in medical, academic, or legal texts; general-public recognition is low.

definition: Moderately neutral slang for cunnilingus; literally 'lick genitals/yin'; 阴 (yīn) refers to female genitalia without the strong vulgarity of 逼 (bī).
notes: 阴 (yīn) also carries cosmological yin/yang associations with the feminine; this term occupies a middle register between clinical 阴部口交 and crude 舔逼; widely understood across demographics.

definition: Extremely crude slang for cunnilingus; literally 'lick pussy/cunt'; 逼 (bī) is one of the most vulgar Mandarin terms for the vulva or vagina.
notes: 逼 (bī) is roughly equivalent in vulgarity to English 'cunt' or 'pussy'; highly offensive in public speech; 逼 also functions as a standalone intensifier and appears in insults such as 傻逼 (stupid cunt).

definition: Slang for cunnilingus; literally 'eat cat'; 猫 (māo, cat) serves as an internet and colloquial euphemism for the vulva, paralleling the English slang use of 'pussy.'
notes: 猫 (cat) is used as a euphemism for female genitalia on Chinese internet platforms; the eating metaphor mirrors 吃屌 (fellatio), creating a symmetrical crude pair; slightly less offensive than 舔逼 because the animal euphemism adds one layer of indirection.
